tweet: Interview Q: Your CISO wants centralized security findings across 50+ AWS accounts. SecurityHub is enabled but findings are scattered. How do you aggregate them for executive reporting? #AWS #CloudSecurity
reply: Enable SecurityHub in a dedicated security account as the aggregator. Use cross-account access to collect findings from all member accounts. Set up EventBridge rules for critical findings. Most miss the custom insights feature for exec summaries.

tweet: Interview question I keep hearing: "You've got 50 AWS accounts. How do you manage IAM across all of them without losing your mind?" Most people blank here. #AWS #DevOps
reply: Real answer: AWS Organizations + SCPs for guardrails, then cross-account roles with external IDs. Don't try to manage each account manually — you'll hate yourself in 6 months. #AWS

tweet: Interview question I keep hearing: "Why would you choose Fargate over EC2?" Most people fumble the answer. The real reason? You're paying for compute you actually use, not idle capacity. But there's a catch most miss.
reply: Fargate shines when you have unpredictable, bursty workloads. Cold starts matter less, scaling's instant. BUT if you're running 24/7 steady-state apps, EC2 Reserved Instances destroy Fargate on cost. Know your workload pattern or you'll burn money.

tweet: Your CloudFormation stack fails with a rollback. You didn't enable termination protection. Now all your resources are gone. How do you prevent this from happening again?
reply: Set DeletionPolicy to Retain on critical resources (databases, S3 buckets). Enable stack termination protection before prod deployments. Also: practice stack updates in staging first — rollbacks happen fast.
